findings.title: release-job-if-disabled matches three literal spellings; other always-false conditions still pass
findings.where: scripts/verify-github-workflows.mjs — isDisabledCondition() and the release-job-if-disabled loop in validateWorkflow()
findings.why: Adversarial copies with `if: 0`, `if: ''`, `if: null`, `if: '${{ 0 }}'` and `if: '${{ ! true }}'` all exit 0 with no issue. At least `${{ 0 }}` and `${{ ! true }}` are always-false expressions under GitHub's expression coercion, so the code comment 'only an always-false value counts' is broader than what is enforced. A maintainer who disables the release with `if: '${{ 0 }}'` gets a green gate and a skipped release — the same failure mode as the closed Medium, though a less likely trigger.
findings.direction: Either extend the finite matcher to the other literal falsy forms (numeric 0, empty string, null, and the obvious constant expressions) with one fixture each, or narrow the comment/doc to the exactly matched spellings. Do not attempt general expression evaluation.
findings.scope: new Nit, outside the frozen direction; the named Medium is CLOSED, not reopened.

findings.title: The new rule's string/expression branches have no shipped self-test control
findings.why: The only job-if fixture uses the YAML boolean `false`. A COPY whose isDisabledCondition() is reduced to `return value === false` still prints 37/37 and accepts the `'false'` and `'${{ false }}'` copies, so a future refactor could drop the string branches without the gate's own self-test noticing. The real gate rejects them today (adversarial matrix), so this is a falsifiability/maintainability gap, not a current runtime hole.
findings.direction: Add fixtures for `if: 'false'` and `if: '${{ false }}'` expecting release-job-if-disabled (or table-drive the three spellings); the count would grow from 37 to 39.
findings.scope: new Nit; the rule itself remains falsifiable (removing the whole block drops the self-test to 36/37).

verdictJustification: Both residual findings are CLOSED with observed evidence — the real gate rejects the boolean, string and expression job-level `if: false` forms while a mutant with only the new block removed accepts them, every new self-test fixture is load-bearing (mutation drops 37/37 to 36/37), the prior five controls still fire, --self-test is 37/37, and the full §3 chain is 11/11 with 325 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail and no secret values — while the two new observations are non-blocking Nits about the matcher's finite spelling scope and the string/expression self-test branches; the real OIDC publish remains unproven until the v0.7.1 tag.
